text:
anya: quick pulse on the mixed-precision bakeoff results? need recommendations for a canary + fallback policy that covers hosted, dedicated, and private customers.

carlos: short summary from our runs yesterday: AWQ-int8 gives the biggest cost win but accuracy delta is noisy on safety prompts. GPTQ-int8 has larger degradation on reasoning tasks. FP8 is closest to baseline but less cost-savings.

li: numbers: MMLU-like eval (paraphrased eval set) — baseline float16 = 100.0, FP8 = 99.6 (+0.4%), AWQ-int8 = 98.9 (+1.1%), GPTQ-int8 = 98.0 (+2.0%). latency (p50 token): baseline fp16 42ms, FP8 36ms, AWQ-int8 48ms, GPTQ 53ms. cost-per-token ratios: AWQ ~0.40x, GPTQ ~0.45x, FP8 ~0.75x vs fp16.

devon: interesting — AWQ is cheaper but latency and quality vary. For hosted, we can route lower-tier customers to AWQ but need strong canary gates. For private/dedicated, we should make defaults conservative and expose quant profiles as opt-in.

anya: proposed canary policy draft — short bullets first then config snippet:
- start with 1% traffic for 24h in hosted on a single region (us-west).
- run the goldenset eval (n=200 prompts across safety, reasoning, retrieval) every hour; compare deltas vs baseline.
- if quality regression > 1.0% absolute on any critical subset OR error rate increase > 0.5%, auto-fallback to FP8 variant for canary traffic and notify oncall.
- staged expansion: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with at least 6h between steps and no gating failures.
- for dedicated/private: require manual opt-in; automated smoke tests + offline eval pass before enabling.

anya: config snippet for rollout engine:

```yaml
policy_name: quant-canary-awq-int8
start_percent: 1
steps: [1, 5, 20, 50, 100]
(step_delay): 6h
quality_gates:
  - name: goldenset_delta
    metric: accuracy_pct
    baseline_ref: model:v2-fp16
    threshold_abs_pct: 1.0
  - name: error_rate
    metric: error_rate_pct
    threshold_abs_pct: 0.5
auto_fallback:
  fallback_model: model:v2-fp8
  triggers: [goldenset_delta, error_rate]
regions: [us-west-2]
profiles: [hosted, dedicated, private]
```

carlos: suggestion: lower the goldenset threshold to 0.75% for safety-related prompts and separate the threshold for LM reasoning benchmarks to 1.5%. Safety regressions are higher impact.

li: agree. here's how our eval subsets performed (quick): safety_delta = +1.6% on AWQ, reasoning_delta = +0.9%, retrieval_delta = +0.3%. So safety is the blocker.

devon: operational concerns: AWQ int8 saw occasional tokenization failures in the tail calls (2 occurrences in 100k calls) — logs attached in the run artifacts. We should add a runtime error_rate gate and a log-level pattern match for "kv-cache-mismatch" to auto-fail the canary.

quant-bot: run-summary: bakeoff-id=2026-03-19-quant-pulse, AWQ-int8 pass_rate=95.8%, FP8 pass_rate=99.1%, GPTQ-int8 pass_rate=93.2%, baseline_fp16=100.0. artifacts_url: https://artifacts.redwood/quant/2026-03-19

anya: thanks — action items:
- li: create a smaller goldenset focusing on safety (n=40) and reasoning (n=60) by EOD.
- carlos: update rollout policy to add separate thresholds for safety vs reasoning and include the kv-cache pattern match.
- devon: run a 24h smoke test on dedicated infra with AWQ-int8 + FP8 fallback and collect tail logs.
- me (anya): draft runbook for oncall auto-fallback + pager thresholds.

carlos: one more ops detail — for private deployments we cannot auto-fallback without customer approval. policy should mark fallback as 'suggested' for private, auto for hosted/dedicated.

li: will also add quantization-specific eval traces so we can diff token-level probabilities for failing examples. helps root cause whether it's quant noise vs tokenizer edge case.

devon: I'll schedule the dedicated smoke tomorrow 02:00 UTC; tagging @sre-bot to monitor infra.

sre-bot: scheduled: dedicated-smoke-awq-2026-03-20 02:00 UTC. monitor alerts: cpu/gpu-temp, kv-cache-errors, rpc-latency. notify: eng-ml-oncall.

anya: perfect. if everyone agrees I'll put the canary policy into the rollout config repo and open a PR with the thresholds we discussed. please thumbs-up or leave comments. :thumbsup: :eyes:

carlos: +1

li: +1

devon: +1

quant-bot: note: remember to include a synthetic prompt set that exercises long-context KV cache (~4k tokens) during the canary step to catch cache mismatch regressions.

anya: good call. adding that to the PR checklist.

carlos: final note — we should store per-customer deployment profile (hosted/dedicated/private) so routing rules can prefer FP8 for high-SLA customers who opt out of experimental quant. avoids surprises.

anya: agreed. closing the thread once PR is up.
